summary:
Radar for 2026-11-04. This snapshot has little fresh randomized head-to-head data: nothing qualifies for an extra L2 long-form under the 48-hour rule. The best opportunities are Lane A practical tirzepatide questions with new news hooks, plus a few emerging research hooks for Shorts.

Main findings:
1. **Long-form queue still on top.** Stopping (SURMOUNT-4), fatigue, injection site, birth control and dehydration remain the highest-value long-forms. Thanksgiving demand peaks Nov 18–27, so Shorts on it need to ship now. The dehydration hook is refreshed by ABC/GMA resurfacing its heat-wave warning (originally July 2026), which suits Australian viewers heading into summer.
2. **Bones and fractures.** A Medscape roundup (Nov 2) says three studies found GLP-1 therapies not linked to higher fracture risk, and a Bone meta-analysis of RCTs came out the same day. This gives a calm "Will tirzepatide weaken my bones?" 08:00 Short. The bones Short is already our second-best (242 views). Caveat: most of this data comes from GLP-1 receptor agonists in type 2 diabetes, not tirzepatide in obesity. The script must say that, and the evidence must not be credited to tirzepatide.
3. **Alcohol is accelerating.** It appeared in two earlier snapshots. This week adds a DOM target-trial emulation including tirzepatide (Nov 3), an EMJ cravings piece (Nov 4) and the BMJ Open emulation (July). It's all observational, so the wording must be "linked to".
4. **Australia's Wegovy pill approval** (Guardian, RACGP, ABC AU, Nov 3–4) is a real AU news spike. My web check could not confirm the TGA decision; the results it returned were from before the approval, so the fact-checker must confirm it on the TGA site. Our data says semaglutide-only titles underperform, so use it only as a "pill vs shot: what's different" Short. Leave out price and supply.
5. **ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17)** is the next scheduled wave: full REDEFINE 4 (CagriSema vs tirzepatide) and possibly retatrutide data. Pre-write "what's confirmed?" Shorts.
6. **Rejected:** affiliate "where to buy" and $99 plans, compounding-network press releases, "research peptide supplier" listicles, "natural GLP-1 alternatives" supplement roundups, and the Celltrion rat-study hype. Gray-market retatrutide (Malaysia seizures, Cureus liver-injury case report) is allowed only as a caution Short, at most one this week.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (783 began the lead-in; 335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88 on placebo, placebo still 9.9% below starting weight)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form (redo shipped 11-04 with defects, so Shorts and IG should now funnel to it): 'Will the weight come back?' answered honestly, then what the trial shows about continuing treatment, plus the habits (protein, strength training) that help. Always include 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own.'
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; extra lift late Dec–Jan (New Year coverage changes and resolutions)
candidates.why_now: Seen in 9 snapshots with rising momentum (82→88). Holiday cost and coverage churn pushes people to search about stopping. IG 'hunger after stopping' is our top Reel (193).

evidence.signal: Randomized withdrawal trial, the core data
Early treatment trajectory and long-term persistence on semaglutide cohort, which gives context on how many people stop

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: getting full fast, protein first, smaller plates, eating slower, alcohol and easing nausea at a big holiday meal
candidates.angle: 08:00 and 20:00 Shorts that funnel to the live Thanksgiving long-form: 'Is it normal to feel full after three bites at Thanksgiving on tirzepatide?' Explain slower stomach emptying, then give a calm plate plan. No weight-centred wording, no restriction messaging.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 9 snapshots with rising momentum (78→83), plus holiday food-industry GLP-1 stories (Starbucks, Times shopping piece, Agweek grocery panel). The seasonal peak is about 2 weeks away; publish Shorts now so they're indexed before it.

evidence.signal: Weight-loss drug users to double as new appetites alter shopping
Digital food purchase signatures change during GLP-1-based treatment

candidates.topic: Why am I so tired on tirzepatide? The Zepbound label lists fatigue in 5% (5 mg), 6% (10 mg) and 7% (15 mg) vs 3% on placebo
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, the next in the queue: 'Is this normal?' Cover the label rates, likely contributors (eating less, fluids, protein, sleep), what helps, and when to call the prescriber. The tone stays calm, not alarmist.
keywords: why am i so tired on mounjaro
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; winter lift Nov–Jan (shorter days, flu season)
candidates.why_now: Seen in 4+ snapshots at 80–82. The Yahoo fatigue piece (Oct 30) is still circulating, and the playbook's Lane A queue names this one. Few videos answer it with the label numbers.

evidence.signal: Fatigue rates by dose vs placebo
'GLP-1s and Fatigue: Why You Feel Tired' mainstream pickup

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: what's normal (redness, itching, small lumps), what the label reports, and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Is this lump normal?' Explain what the label reports, why it happens, the label's guidance on rotating sites, and the signs that need a call. Use a calm neutral mascot, no graphic images. Its Short reached 179 views on day 1.
keywords: is a red bump normal after zepbound
candidates.why_now: Seen in 6 snapshots. The 08:00 Short started stronger than any since hair (179 on day 1), which shows real demand, and no Lane A long-form answers it yet.

evidence.signal: Injection site reaction rates vs placebo

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and dehydration: signs and what helps. The label warns of acute kidney injury linked to dehydration from vomiting or diarrhoea. Hook: ABC/GMA doctors' GLP-1 heat warning resurfaced Nov 4 (first published July 2026), with an Australian summer and US winter-illness angle
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Why am I always thirsty, or never thirsty, on tirzepatide?' Explain that appetite and thirst cues can drop, list the warning signs from the label's kidney section, and give practical fluid habits. Also link sick days.
candidates.predicted_peak: AU summer Dec–Feb; US flu season Dec–Jan
candidates.why_now: ABC/GMA put the heat-wave piece back in the news feed today. Australian viewers are heading into summer, and the playbook queue lists this topic.

evidence.source: Good Morning America / ABC (July 2026, resurfaced Nov 4)
evidence.signal: Doctors warn GLP-1 users about dehydration in heat; some people have reduced thirst
Local pickup of dehydration warning
Acute kidney injury warning linked to dehydration from GI side effects

candidates.topic: Will tirzepatide weaken my bones? Three studies report GLP-1 therapies not linked to higher fracture risk (Medscape, Nov 2), plus a Bone meta-analysis of placebo-controlled RCTs on bone metabolism (Nov 2)
candidates.angle: 08:00 body-worry reassurance Short that funnels to the live Bones & Muscle long-form. Give the honest answer: fracture data so far is reassuring but mostly observational and in type 2 diabetes. Name the population. The muscle and bone habits (protein, resistance training) are the new fact.
candidates.why_now: New Medscape roundup (Nov 2) and Bone meta-analysis (Nov 2). The bones Short is our second-best (242), and Bones & Muscle needs traffic. Mainstream consumer coverage hasn't caught up yet.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 therapies not linked to increased fracture risk in three studies
Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs of GLP-1 RAs on bone metabolism (mostly first-generation agents)
134,000 adults with T2D: GLP-1 RA linked to 21% lower fragility fracture risk vs DPP-4 (observational)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and birth control pills: what the label says about reduced oral contraceptive exposure, refreshed by the Front Pharmacol pregnancy-outcomes meta-analysis (Oct 16)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, label only: why the stomach-emptying effect matters for pills, what the label says around starting and dose increases, and to ask your prescriber about contraception. No instructions.
candidates.why_now: Queued in the playbook and seen in 3+ snapshots. New pregnancy meta-analysis and ACOG guidance keep it in the news. Searches are high among women 25–45, a large part of the tirzepatide audience.

evidence.signal: Pregnancy and perinatal outcomes after GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP exposure, meta-analysis
Oral contraceptive interaction section

candidates.topic: Do GLP-1 medicines change how much you want to drink? A DOM target-trial emulation of semaglutide and tirzepatide and alcohol-related outcomes in type 2 diabetes (Nov 3), the EMJ cravings report (Nov 4) and a BMJ Open emulation (22–32% lower alcohol-related hospitalisation, observational)
candidates.angle: 13:00 Short with tirzepatide named first: 'Lost your taste for wine on tirzepatide? Here's what studies link it to.' Present it strictly as 'linked to' observational data, and note that alcohol can worsen nausea and blood-sugar effects. Not a treatment claim for alcohol use disorder.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots and accelerating: a new peer-reviewed study (Nov 3), EMJ coverage (Nov 4), and beer-sales business stories. Holiday drinking season starts now.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide, tirzepatide and recorded alcohol-related outcomes in T2D: target-trial emulation
Newer obesity drugs linked to fewer alcohol-related hospitalisations in alcohol dependence (40,703 adults)
GLP-1 receptor agonists cut alcohol cravings

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines vs metformin in prediabetes with obesity: AHA Scientific Sessions observational study of more than 250,000 adults (31% lower risk of type 2 diabetes; more people returning to normal blood sugar), now in Newsweek (Nov 4)
candidates.angle: 13:00 Short: 'Prediabetes and considering tirzepatide or semaglutide? What a 250,000-person study found.' Use the observational wording, give absolute context where available, say metformin isn't 'bad', and add a talk-to-your-prescriber line. S2 11-04 already covered prediabetes, so use a new fact (heart attack and stroke figures) and a different angle.
candidates.why_now: Moved from AHA press (Nov 2) to Cardiovascular Business, Medical Xpress and now Newsweek (Nov 4). Mainstream pickup is underway. Seen in 2 snapshots (78→84).

evidence.signal: GLP-1 meds linked to lower diabetes, heart risks than standard diabetes prevention med
GLP-1 users saw lower risks of heart attack and stroke in major study

candidates.topic: Australia approves its first GLP-1 weight-loss pill (oral semaglutide, Wegovy tablet; TGA, reported Nov 3–4): how it differs from injections and who may be eligible
candidates.angle: 13:00 Short for AU and UK viewers: 'Pill vs injection: what's actually different?' Cover daily vs weekly dosing, taking it on an empty stomach as the label describes (no dose talk), and trial results compared with injections only as 'separate trials'. No price, supply or 'where to get it'. Don't use an 'Approved yet?' frame.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–5 days (AU news cycle), second wave at AU launch around Christmas
candidates.why_now: Guardian, RACGP newsGP, ABC AU, The Conversation, Australian Pharmacist and The Australian all covered it within 24 h. Novo's earnings (Nov 4) spotlight Wegovy pill demand. AU is a high-CPM market.

evidence.signal: Australia's first GLP-1 weight-loss pill approved: how it differs and who is eligible
TGA approves Wegovy weight-loss pill
How the Wegovy pill compares with injections

candidates.topic: ObesityWeek 2026 (Nov 14–17): full REDEFINE 4 results, CagriSema vs tirzepatide in adults with obesity (open-label, 84 weeks; topline about 23% with CagriSema, non-inferiority to tirzepatide not met), plus possible retatrutide Phase 3 presentations
candidates.angle: Pre-plan for the 13:00 slot: a tirzepatide-first head-to-head Short ('Tirzepatide vs CagriSema: what the full results confirm') with a loop ending, published within 48 h of the presentation. If a peer-reviewed head-to-head drops, this is the only route to an extra L2 long-form.
candidates.why_now: A scheduled catalyst. The head-to-head is in an obesity population with tirzepatide named first, our best Short format (107–173 views). Seen in 2 snapshots.

What new weight-loss drugs are coming? Mainstream pipeline interest

candidates.topic: Menopause hormone therapy and tirzepatide: Mayo Clinic observational data linking HT with more weight lost (about 19.2% vs 14% on tirzepatide alone), back in the news via Newsweek (Nov 3)
candidates.angle: 20:00 or 13:00 Short: 'Does hormone therapy change how tirzepatide works?' The main point is that it's observational and not randomized, and that this is a conversation for your doctor, not a reason to start HT. Don't call it new; the study was published in early 2026.
candidates.why_now: Newsweek resurfaced it (Nov 3) and it has had repeated waves of coverage. Women 45–65 are a core audience segment. Our menopause Shorts have underperformed (58), so it ranks medium.

evidence.signal: Menopausal hormone therapy linked to greater weight loss with tirzepatide
Hormone therapy linked to how some women respond to GLP-1 drugs

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide real-world results at 12 months (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 28): clinically meaningful weight reduction outside trials
candidates.angle: 20:00 funnel Short: 'Do real-world tirzepatide results match the trials?' Compare it with SURMOUNT-1 as separate studies, not head-to-head, and explain why staying on treatment and habits matter. Funnel to How Long or Plateau.

evidence.signal: Tirzepatide 12-month real-world weight reduction in obesity or overweight

candidates.angle: 08:00 'Is this normal?' Short: 'Sick with a stomach bug on tirzepatide?' Cover fluids, label-based signs of dehydration, and when to call the prescriber. No dose-skipping advice. Use a different angle from S1 11-04 (sick days), for example cold-medicine questions for the pharmacist.

Keep each signal attached to its drug.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs and the eye: ocular safety, retinal outcomes
